chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Ubaydi, from Hammad ibn Isa who said:

I entered upon Abi al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) and said to him: May I be your ransom, supplicate to Allah for me that He grants me a house, a wife, a son, a servant, and Hajj every year. He (peace be upon him) said: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and grant him a house, a wife, a son, a servant, and Hajj for fifty years. Hammad said: So when he specified fifty years, I knew that I would not perform Hajj more than fifty years. Hammad also said: I performed Hajj for forty-eight years, and this is my house which I have been granted, and this is my wife behind the veil hearing my speech, and this is my son, and this is my servant, I have been granted all that…

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common phrase of respect in supplication)

ai.seo_question: What did Hammad ibn Isa ask Imam al-Rida for, and how did the Imam's response regarding 'fifty years' come to pass?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Rijal al-Kashi*, Hammad ibn Isa requests specific worldly provisions from Imam al-Rida (AS), who responds with a prayer for fifty years of these blessings. Hammad interprets the specific number 'fifty' as a divine limit on his lifespan or capacity for Hajj, a prediction he verifies by performing Hajj for forty-eight years and retaining all other requested blessings. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s knowledge of the unseen (*Ilm al-Ghayb*) and the spiritual significance of specific numerical signs in divine decrees.
